en: Now, sometimes you just have a quick
question for Py or something you wanna
explore where you don't wanna create a
session. So where you don't wanna get an
entry in that resume dropdown so that you
don't pollute your sessions.
This can especially be useful if you run Py
globally to quickly find a file on your
system or anything like that.
In situations like this, you can run Py with
the --nosession flag,
--nosession. This runs Py like always
and you can use it with any whatever flags
you may have added or you may wanna add.
But this session here
is not stored on disk. That's the main
difference. So
if I ask it, what can you do for me
here?
It will process this, it will
reply, and it could also edit files and so
on. It's a regular session. It can do what
it can always do.
But you will notice that once it's done,
If I quit
and then start Py with the resume picker,
that session we just had is not here because
it was not stored on disk. And that can
sometimes be useful and nice to have.
